params.body:
Shane, on the "Zoek gemiddelde verkoopprijs eindklant" modal: "mss bij gemiddelde zoekprijs berekenen, alle inputs aantal tussen haken tonen?" And: "kunnen we bij zoek gemiddelde verkoopprijs ook test toevoegen?"

## What changed

**Counts on every select.** Make and model already showed "VW (19)", "T-Roc (2)". Transmission, fuel, category and body style now do the same, computed the same way. The component holds one table of facets (`FACETS`: select to vehicle column) and one of what each select leaves out of its own count (`COUNTS_WITHOUT`); the view renders every select from the same option shape.

**The counting convention, as found on make and model and now applied to all six.** A select counts the population *within the other selects*, never within itself, and not within the select that depends on it: make is counted without the chosen model (a model implies its make), category without the chosen body style. Model counts within the chosen make; body style within the chosen category. Concretely, with make VW and manual chosen: the transmission select still says "Automaat (6)" (it does not count itself), fuel and category count within VW plus manual.

**"Alle" carries a count.** The make select already showed "Alle (30)"; model did not. Now every select does: the total you get without a choice there (the pool within the other selects). This follows make, the primary sibling.

**Zero.** Make and model both left an option with count 0 out of the list rather than showing "(0)", and kept the currently chosen option even at zero so the select never loses its value. The four new selects do the same. Pinned in the test: a fuel nothing carries is absent; the chosen fuel stays as "Benzine (0)" and the result says "geen wagens".

**Performance.** The existing two counts were not N+1: one `extendedSearch` query for the pool (plus its eager load of `portals.portal`), then `countBy` in memory. That pool was, however, filtered in SQL by the four other selects, which is why they could not be counted from it. Now the population is fetched once with only period and variant (`population()`), and every narrowing is in memory (`narrow()`): six counts, one query, the same as before when nothing was chosen. The pool is a year of sales across all dealers; that is what it already loaded in the common case.

## What the tests pin about the calculation (R S1-5.14, R S1-5.15)

Every expected number is a literal in the test.

- **Average, minimum, maximum**: 10 000, 12 000, 17 000 gives "€ 13 000,00", "tussen € 10 000,00 en € 17 000,00", "op basis van 3".
- **Population**: the sale date in the period is the marker; the `sold` flag is not read (every sale path writes the three fields together, `Sale::sold()` / `Sale::unsold()`). An unsold vehicle of the same make and model is out. The day exactly twelve months back is **out** (`whereDate(sold_at, '>', now - 12 months)`), the day after is in, today is in.
- **A sale without a price counts as 0**: it lowers the average and becomes the minimum ("tussen € 0,00 en ..."). Pinned as it is; recorded as **X-128** (deze week, Ilse) because a dealer who registers a sale without a price lowers everyone's market reference.
- **Whose vehicles**: all non-demo dealers, the dealer's own sales included; vehicles that were on the bidding platform are out. The rule said "collega-wagens": rule and code disagree, so the rule now says what the code does and **X-129** (later, Ilse) asks whether the own dealer belongs in.
- **Each filter narrows**: year from/to, km from/to, transmission, fuel, category, body style, one assertion each.
- **Histogram (R S1-5.15)**: spans the population within the selects and the chosen period, and ignores the year and mileage bounds (a bound cuts the result and dispatches no new histogram). The rule said "a fixed 12-month window"; that described the deleted `OwnStockController::averagePriceHistogram`. The Livewire component follows the chosen period (the histogram key carries `months`), which is the intent of the rewrite, so the rule text is corrected rather than filed as a finding.

## Two defects found on the way, both fixed in the files of this PR

- **X-127** The trader variant (bidding page, `merchant: true`) ran on `export_bids.*` rows without a single vehicle column. Make and model counted on a column that did not exist (every make hidden, a chosen make gave "no vehicles"), the histogram had nothing to show; only the four other selects worked because they filtered in SQL. With in-memory narrowing they would have gone too. `extendedSearch` now selects the six facet columns plus construction year and mileage of the vehicle onto the bid row. This component is the only caller with `merchant`; `strict` is off so the group by on the bid row allows it. Test: bids count and narrow by make.
- **X-130** The year and mileage bounds were cleared *after* the result was cut, so the response that changed a select or the period still filtered on the bounds it had just cleared and could say "geen wagens verkocht" until the next interaction. The reset now comes before the cut; the histogram test caught it.

## The phone size

The selects carried `form-control form-control-sm`, not `ui-select`; `.wf-veld .form-control` (specificity 0,2,0) would also have beaten the `.ui-select` rule of PR 347. They now carry `ui-select` alone (same 13 px on a wide screen, 38 px instead of 36 px high), so the 16 px / 44 px rule of PR 347 reaches them once that lands. No font-size rule added here; `refresh.css` untouched.

## Rules

R S1-5.14 rewritten with the population, the period edge, the counting convention, the zero behaviour and the trader variant; R S1-5.15 with the period and the reset order; both point at `AveragePriceSearch` (the controller methods they named no longer exist). X-127 to X-130 added to `90-x-bevindingen.md` (X-125 and X-126 were taken on main while this was written).

## Verified

`vendor/bin/phpunit --filter 'AveragePrice|OwnStockList|StylesheetSyntax|AlpineExpression|RulesCoverage'`: OK (30 tests, 724 assertions). Neighbours `VehicleFilterInjection|Export|Bidding|StocklistBrowser|Smoke`: OK (158 tests). Rendered in the running app with a seeded set (30 sales, three makes) at 1440 px and 390 px; with VW chosen the selects read "Alle (30) | Audi (7) | BMW (4) | VW (19)", "Alle (19) | Caddy (5) | Golf (12) | T-Roc (2)", "Alle (19) | Manueel (13) | Automaat (6)", "Alle (19) | Benzine (5) | Diesel (14)", "Alle (19) | Personenwagen (14) | Bestelwagen (5)".
params.title: The average-price search counts on every select, and the calculation is pinned
